 Camps

 Discover Kanawana

 Camp YMCA Kanawana: Summer Camp Experience in the Laurentians

 Since 1894, Camp YMCA Kanawana has been welcoming generations of campers. Kanawana offers a screen-free experience in the heart of nature where campers will enjoy something truly special: days spent paddling on the lake, exploring the woods, and falling asleep under the stars, all while making lasting friendships with other campers.

 Mutual support, a love of nature, and inclusion—once your child has experienced the magic of Kanawana, you will understand why campers do not come back out of habit, but because they have discovered a place where they truly belong.

 Discover our camp programs 

 Registration for the 2027 season at YMCA Kanawana Camp is about to open!  

 Fill out the interest form 

 Registration 2027

 Registration for the 2027 season at YMCA Kanawana Camp is about to open!

 Fill out the interest form to stay tuned for updates.

 An Experience That Makes a Lasting Impression

 A safe environment where campers feel confident learning

 While your child is living out their adventure, you can rest easy.

 A founding member of the Association des camps du Québec (ACQ), Kanawana is renowned for its high standards of supervision and its extensively trained staff (over 80 hours of training).

 ● ACQ- and YMCA Canada-certified camp

 ● Ratio of 1 adult for 3 campers

 ● Activity leaders, lifeguards, and trip guides certified by recognized organizations

 ● On-site infirmary open 24 hours per day

 An English-speaking environment where everyone is welcome

 At camp, your child will be immersed in an English-speaking environment.

 Even if they are not fully comfortable speaking English, campers quickly find their bearings, fully participate in activities, and build self-confidence throughout their stay.

 ● Mostly bilingual staff (French and English)

 ● No English proficiency required to register

 Non nobis solum: learning to think of others

 Kanawana’s motto—non nobis solum (not for ourselves alone)—is part of everyday life at camp.

 Guided by the values of caring, solidarity, boldness, and respect, campers learn to push themselves while watching out for others and discover that they are capable of so much more than they ever imagined.

 ● Self-confidence and pushing one’s limits

 ● Team spirit and solidarity

 ● Sense of responsibility

 Nature as our adventure playground

 Imagine three private lakes, forests for miles, and campfires under the stars.

 Archery, rock climbing, canoeing, nature interpretation, and woodworking … here campers spend their summers outdoors for a screen-free experience.

 ● Water activities on private lake

 ● Arts, music, and creativity

 ● 4- to 28-day canoe trips

 A Camp in the Heart of Nature

 Discover the Site and Facilities 

 Located in the heart of the Laurentians, just one hour from Montréal and 10 minutes from the town of Saint-Sauveur, Camp YMCA Kanawana is a summer camp located in the heart of nature where campers can disconnect from the everyday and enjoy a memorable summer.

 The camp sits on a historic site surrounded by private lakes and forests. It offers a safe, supervised environment where each camper can explore, be active, and thrive.

 Discover the facilities 

 Testimonials

 I attended Camp Kanawana at the end of the 1960s […]. My daughter went towards the end of the 1990s, and I’m proud to say that my grandson just spent his first summer there […]. I think Kanawana is one of the best summer camps in Québec (if not the best). Kids are responsibly supervised, but they also have the chance to develop their independence […]. The stories and memories they bring home are incredible. 
 
 Dee

 My son went to Camp Kanawana last summer for one week. His first time at a sleep away camp. He loved it so much he said it ‘was the best week of his life!’ Lol. He loved the activities, the food, everything. He has been talking about it ever since and has his photos with his camp group up on the wall next to his bed. 
 
 Sheena

 I would definitely recommend Kanawana to younger kids, because your counsellor cares for you so much, and they do everything with you. They’re your first friend at Kanawana. 
 
 Xavier

 Counsellor | Canoe Trip Guide, and Former Camper

 YMCA Kanawana Summer Camp Programs

 Camp Stays: On-Site Programs

 Every day at camp is a new adventure. We sing around the campfire, take on challenges in the woods, discover hidden talents, and create memories that last a lifetime.

 Categories of activities 

 Water sports: water trampoline, swimming, paddle boarding, kayaking, canoeing
 Sports and recreation: ropes course, archery, rock climbing, soccer, gaga ball
 Arts and more: theatre, music, arts and crafts, dance, woodworking, survival skills, nature exploration
 
 Each activity is devised to develop new skills, stimulate creativity, encourage outdoor exploration, and create lasting friendship, all in the unique Kanawana spirit.

 Camp Stays for Younger Kids

 Girls and non-binary (Ages 7 to 12)
 
 6-Day Pioneers 

 Boys and non-binary (Ages 7 to 12)
 
 6-Day Woodsies 

 Girls and non-binary (Ages 7 to 12)
 
 12-Day Pioneers

 12-Day Woodsies 

 Camp Stays for Teens

 Girls and non-binary (Ages 13 to 16)
 
 12-Day Pathfinders 

 Boys and non-binary (Ages 13 to 16)
 
 12-Day Coureurs des bois 

 Canoe Trips

 Want to take it a step further? Our canoe trips are designed for young people with a thirst for adventure.

Guided by our experienced team, campers learn to paddle, set up camp, and live in the great outdoors, surrounded by breathtaking scenery.

Sleeping under the stars, cooking together, sharing stories around the campfire… Every expedition becomes a highlight of the summer.

Beyond the adventure, campers develop independence, team spirit, and self-confidence through an immersive and unforgettable experience.

 Canoe-tripping for younger campers:

 Girls and non-binary (Ages 11 to 12)
 
 12-Day Explorers Pioneers 

 Boys and non-binary (Ages 11 to 12)
 
 12-Day Explorers Woodsies 

 Canoe-tripping for teens:

 Girls and non-binary (Ages 13 to 16)
 
 12-Day Adventurers Pathfinders 

 Boys and non-binary (Ages 13 to 16)
 
 12-Day Adventurers Coureurs des Bois 

 Mixed (Ages 13 to 16)
 
 12-Day Voyageurs 

 mixed (Ages 14 to 17)
 
 19-Day Voyageurs Extreme 

 Application to Leadership Programs

 Camp YMCA Kanawana offers an environment that is perfect for developing leadership skills and promotes learning through experience, responsibility, adventure, and friendship.

Whether teens want to become counsellors, canoe trip guides, or program coordinators, we have the perfect program to match their aspirations. Teens will develop new childcare, program planning, and survival skills. (Prerequisite: completion of grade 10/secondary 4.)

Financial assistance and camperships are also available for our leadership programs.

 Apply for a leadership program

 Our Leadership Programs

 Mixed (Ages 15 to 16)

 Mixed (Ages 16 to 17)

 FAQ

 What does a typical day at camp look like? 

 In regular camp programs, campers spend most of their day with their cabin/tent group and counsellors. They eat meals together, choose activities as a group, and do their bedtime routine together. In the afternoons, they are scheduled for two blocks of what we call “Interest Groups,” where they get to choose their own two activities for one week at a time, apart from their bunkmates. 

 Campers get to choose other activities or spend time with their friends in other sections or cabins/tents during “General Swim” time twice a day.

 What is the food like? Do you cater to special diets? 

 Our chef works closely with a dietician to ensure that our meals are varied and healthy for growing kids. 

 Meals are served at the table “family style,” meaning that our staff can oversee how their campers eat during every meal. 

 We serve three meals a day, offer fruit and water throughout the day as an extra boost, and snacks most evenings. 

 We also accommodate vegetarian, lactose-free, as well as and pork- or beef-free diets. We do not serve any products with nuts, and do our best to ensure that none are brought onto the camp – but we cannot guarantee a 100% nut-free environment. 

 For dietary restrictions other than those listed above, you can always contact the camp director to discuss your options; working with our chef, we should be able to find a way to accommodate your camper!

 How can I communicate with my camper while they are at camp? 

 Campers can communicate with their parents via good old-fashioned snail mail, and once a week we offer to scan and email a letter home for every child on site; campers on canoe trips will not have this option. Parents can communicate with their children by sending an email that will be printed and delivered once a day, or letters by regular mail, or even packages through Canada Post or UPS/FedEx (we do not recommend Purolator, as they don’t always deliver directly to camp). 

 When sending packages, PLEASE do not include food or candy, because they attract various critters into the tents and cabins. Please note that the post office is responsible for delivery times and there may be significant delays. We recommend sending one letter or two before your camper arrives at camp, so that they can get them sooner! More information on how communication works can be found in our Parent Guide online.

 If there is an emergency, how can I contact the camp? 

 Should there be an urgent need for you to contact the camp directly, you can always call the camp phone line and our office staff will connect you to the appropriate person, i.e. the camp director, your camper’s section director, or even set a time to speak to your camper directly. 

 Also, any child who has a birthday while they are at camp gets to call home.

 What are your policies regarding swimming/water safety? 

 All campers are evaluated in the water during their first couple of days at camp. This evaluation will determine whether they can swim in the shallow or the deep end of our designated swimming area, and whether or not they can use our boating equipment on their own, or need to be accompanied by a staff member. 

 The children can be re-evaluated anytime throughout their stay to obtain their “blue cord,” which would allow them to swim in the deep end and go boating on their own. All participants must wear a PFD when using water equipment outside the designated swimming area (water trampoline, canoes, kayaks, SUPs).

 What if my camper has another obligation during the session? Can I register them for only part of a session? 

 If your camper needs to leave camp for a specific reason, i.e. a medical appointment, school exam, sports try-out, etc., you can contact the camp staff and schedule a short absence and pick them up and drop them off accordingly. You can communicate with the camp director or section director directly to make arrangements. 

 We do not offer partial sessions as such, because the remaining portion could not be filled by another camper, and so it would be a spot taken away from someone who wanted to be at the camp for the entire two-week period. If necessary, you can drop your camper off late, or pick them up early, but we do not recommend doing so as they would miss out on of the full camp experience!

 Where and when are the pick-up and drop-off times for the bus? 

 Our buses offer round-trip transportation from Pierre LaPorte High School in Town of Mount Royal (1101 Rockland Road). For departures to camp, you should arrive at the school between 7 a.m. and 8 a.m. on the Monday when camp starts. 

 Campers will return between 4 p.m. and 6 p.m. on the Friday the session ends. For further details regarding pick-ups and drop-offs, please consult our Parent Guide online.

 What is the “tuck fee” for? 

 Every camper who comes to Kanawana will receive a water bottle on their first day at camp to ensure that they stay hydrated throughout their stay. Upon leaving, they will also get a camp t-shirt and photos with both their group and with the whole camp to take home as souvenirs; a portion of the tuck fee covers the cost of those items. 

 The remaining balance of the tuck fee remains in their account to spend at the camp’s “tuck shop,” where we have additional camp-related swag items and other useful things like toothbrushes, flashlights, batteries, or stamps to mail letters home and even a few snacks. Your camper can also use the money in their account to buy items from the camp store, and any unused funds at the end of their stay can either be refunded upon request, or simply be put towards our campership fund for future seasons. 

 You can request for additional funds to be added to their camp store account as needed; they start off with $30 to spend at the store.

 Where do the campers sleep? 

 Campers in the Junior sections (Woodsmen and Pioneers) sleep in cabins that accommodate 10, with 2 staff members in their own small room within that cabin. There are six upper bunks and four lower bunks, with cubbies for each camper to store their personal stuff for daily use. Their duffel bag/suitcase/trunk goes under their bed and holds most of their clothing. Every camper bed has its own window and the cabin has a front-covered porch for hanging things up to dry, or simply for keeping shoes outside the main cabin room.

 Campers in the Senior sections (Coureurs des Bois, Pathfinders, Rangers, Trailblazers, Voyageurs, Foresters and Adventurers) sleep in platform tents, namely a wooden platform with bunk beds, covered by a heavy canvas tent and waterproof tarp. This group consists of 8 campers and 1 to 2 staff members all sharing the same space. There are clothes lines for hanging things to dry, as well as some shelves for storing items of daily use. During the day, campers are encouraged to roll up their tent walls to let the air flow freely and then roll them down at night to keep the bugs away and stay warm.

 How are counsellors selected for the different groups? 

 Counsellors are assigned to groups based on their abilities and experience. Junior counsellors having their first experience with campers will always be paired with an older, more experienced counsellor for their first session.

 Counsellors are always at least 3 years older than the campers they supervise, as per ACQ (Association des camps du Québec) guidelines. The Pathfinders and Pioneers groups are made up of girls and non-binary campers; Coureurs des Bois and Woodsmen consist of boys and non-binary campers; Senior Kanawanians and Voyageurs are co-ed groups. Staff are not assigned based on gender identity, but if your camper needs to be placed with counsellors of their own gender identity exclusively, you may contact the camp director and make that request.

 How do I know which trip option is right for my camper? 

 The Explorers program is a short trip across flat water (lakes and hiking) for 11- and 12-year-old campers. It is a great option for beginners to gain experience, though for safety reasons, we do require that these campers be strong swimmers, i.e. able to get their “blue cord” during the swimming evaluation.

 The Adventurers programs are shorter canoe trips for campers aged 13 to 16. Sessions 1 through 3 are  white water (river) trips, and session 4 is a flat water outing. As with Explorers, Adventurers should be confident swimmers but do not need vast canoeing experience to take part in these trips. We recommend these programs to older campers as a first canoe-camping experience or to campers who have participated in the Explorers program but have never been on a white water excursion. 

 If your camper already has some canoeing experience, then the Voyageurs program is the one for them. This trip is open to campers aged 13 to 16 as well, but lasts 8 days, as opposed to only 4 or 5 days as the others. Sessions 1 through 3 are white-water (river) trips, and session 4 is a flat water (lake) outing. Voyageurs should be strong swimmers and we recommend that they have some experience with canoes.

 Voyageur Ultimate is a much longer, white-water adventure lasting 26 days, for relatively experienced (or VERY adventurous!) teens aged 15 to 17.

 Campers with Different Needs 

 Camp YMCA Kanawana is an inclusive community that strives to welcome youth with different needs and diverse abilities.

 However, our camp is located in a natural setting and features uneven terrain. As our resources are limited, it is preferable that campers can participate in daily activities with minimal support.

 To help us assess the needs of your child, please write to  wellness.kanawana@ymcaquebec.org to get a participation request form. 

 Once you return the completed form, we will be able to determine whether we can provide the assistance required. 

 Please note that the number of companions per session is limited.

 Discover Kanawana

 The Kanawana Story

 Camp YMCA Kanawana’s History

 Since 1894, Camp YMCA Kanawana has been welcoming generations of campers in a beautiful natural setting that encourages learning new skills, developing a sense of leadership, and making friends. Discover the major milestones that have marked the camp's history. 

 1894 – In the beginning

 In the summer of 1894, "Billy" Ball of the YMCA of Montréal took a group of boys to camp on an island in Lake St. Joseph, in the Township of Howard, near Sainte-Agathe, Québec. Billy's concept was to take youth away from the hustle and bustle of everyday life and to teach them about group dynamics, team building, and leadership. This program was so successful that the YMCA of Montréal purchased the island (in addition to two others) and used them for leadership training. In 1894, Camp Jubilee, Québec's first residential summer camp, opened with a total registration of 20 campers.

 1910 – Creation of Camp Kanawana

 Looking for a larger site, the YMCA acquired a site in Saint-Sauveur from the Page family. Camp Kanawana opened its doors and 85 campers registered for the first session.

 1947 – Creation of the Lumbermen and Voyageur Games

 The games were inspired by Pinecrest Camp and quickly became an annual Kanawana tradition. In 2025, the games will celebrate their 78th edition.  

 1968 – Kanawana starts to welcome girl campers

 Kawanana welcomed girls to its camp for the first time, beginning a long tradition of inclusion and diversity.  

 2022 – Launch of the Mountaineer program

 The Mountaineer program was launched as an all gender tent to provide a safe and welcoming environment for transgender, non-binary, and gender non-conforming campers.

 2025 – Camp Kanawana's 131st season

 YMCA Kanawana celebrates 131 years of history and 148 years of the YMCA's commitment to residential camps and to training the leaders of tomorrow.

 Discover Kanawana

 Parents' Guide

 Parent Information Package and Packing Guides

 Are you getting your child ready for a stay at Camp YMCA Kanawana   ? Here are all the essential documents to help you plan their stay and have a stress-free packing experience. 

 Preparation Guide

 This document presents all the useful information to get your camper ready for their stay: camp programs, transportation, communications, and policies.

 Kanawana 2026 - Parent Information Package 

 Packing Guide

 To ensure your child fully enjoys their camp experience, we recommend consulting the list of articles to pack according to the program they are registered for. This guide includes a general list and a version adapted for canoe-tripping programs.

 Kanawana - Packing Guide 

 Kanawana - Trip Packing Guide 

 Leaders in Training Information Guide

 Participating in a Leaders-in-Training (LIT) program? This guide will help you get ready for your training so you have a rewarding leadership experience.

 Leaders in Training Information Guide

 Camp YMCA Kanawana’s history

 Camps

 Discover Kanawana

 12-Day Adventurers Coureurs des bois (Ages 13-16)

 12-Day Adventurers Coureurs des bois

 Campers aged 13 to 16 experience their first canoe-tripping adventure, combining life at Camp YMCA Kanawana with a four- to six-day trip in the wilderness . 

 Before setting out, they take part in a range of camp activities while developing the skills they will need for their trip. 

 Led by experienced guides, they are introduced to canoe tripping, build independence and learn to take on challenges and work as a team in a natural setting.  

 2027 Registration

 Ages: 13 to 16

 Gender: boy and non-binary

 Registration for the 2027 season at YMCA Kanawana Camp is about to open!

 Fill out the interest form

 Previous element 

 Next element 

 How to register

 Only available during registration period.

 Step 1: Click on the "Register your child" button

 Step 2: Once you have chosen the age-appropriate program for your child, create or log in to your account on Active, our registration and payment platform, and add your child's profile to your account.

 Step 3: Complete the transaction on Active. 

 If you need help, please write to us using our contact form or call us at 514-687-9622 , ext. 1524 (Montréal) or 1-833-505-9622, ext. 1524 (outside Montréal). 

 Opening hours
 Monday - Friday* : 8 a.m. - 7 p.m. 
 Saturday* : 9 a.m. - 4 p.m.
 Sunday* : 10 a.m. - 4 p.m.
 View the itinerary 

 Our address

 673 Saint-Elmire Street
Saint-Sauveur-des-Monts, QC, J0R 1R1

 Phone numbers

 1 833 505-9622 
 514 687-9622 

 Email

 camp.kanawana@ymcaquebec.org 

 *Opening hours of the Contact Centre 

 Additional information

 Learn more about the program 

 Campers spend most days in our Regular Residential Camp program while also preparing and training for their 4- to 6-day canoe trip.

 All our canoe trips are centred on teamwork and community living while helping participants develop their leadership and outdoor survival skills.

 Please note: For safety purposes, Camp YMCA Kanawana reserves the right to change the length and locations of each trip. These will be determined depending on weather, water, and road conditions, as well as the overall schedule of trips each session.

 Canoe trips are physically demanding and require a certain level of swimming ability. Kanawana therefore reserves the right to refuse any participant we deem unable to cope with the demands of such a trip.

 * If your child is gender non-conforming or transgender, please let us know so that we can ensure that they are comfortable with their cabin arrangement.

 A typical day at camp YMCA Kanawana 

 This is a typical day on a canoe -camping trip:
7 a.m.: wake-up
7:30 a.m.: participation in tasks that will also need to be done on the trip, such as gathering firewood and making breakfast
9 a.m.: take down tents and camp site and help pack canoes
10:30 a.m.: paddle
11:30 a.m.: canoe games and rest
12:30 p.m.: lunch on the beach
2 p.m.: paddle to camp site
3 p.m.: put up tents and swimming by camp site
4 p.m.: survival program activity     
5:30 p.m.: dinner preparation and participation in trip tasks
7:30 p.m.: stories around the campfire
9 p.m.: teeth brushing and sweet dreams

 Please note that this is a generic schedule that will be adapted to each program by our trip guides according to the group's itinerary. 

 Financial assistance 

 All young people should have the opportunity to experience the magic of camp, regardless of their financial situation. 

 That is why our financial assistance program can cover part of the cost if you are unable to pay the full amount. 

 Tax credits 

 Some fees are eligible for tax credits for child care expense and children’s physical activities. If you would like to receive the tax credit for child care expenses by advance payments , please consult the detailed procedure on the Revenu Québec website before contacting us. Certain conditions apply.

 Terms and conditions 

 Consult our terms and conditions to learn about our refund policies, Camp YMCA Kanawana registration modifications, as well as the general terms and conditions you agree to when you register your child for camp.

 Previous element 

 Next element 

 Find out more about YMCA Kanawana camp

 All our practical advice for your stay at camp.

 Camp YMCA Kanawana offers a gorgeous natural setting.

 Camps

 Discover Kanawana

 12-Day Adventurers Pathfinders (Ages 13-16)

 12-Day Adventurers Pathfinders

 Campers aged 13 to 16 are introduced to canoe tripping through an experience that combines life at Camp YMCA Kanawana with a four-day trip in the wilderness .  

 Led by experienced guides, they gradually prepare for their trip while developing their canoeing skills, independence and team spirit.  

 This adventure is designed to help them take on new challenges and enjoy a rewarding outdoor experience. 

 Learn more about the program 

 2027 Registration

 Ages: 13 to 16

 Gender: girl and non-binary

 Registration for the 2027 season at YMCA Kanawana Camp is about to open!

 Fill out the interest form

 Previous element 

 Next element 

 How to register

 Only available during registration period.

 Step 1: Click on the "Register your child" button

 Step 2: Once you have chosen the age-appropriate program for your child, create or log in to your account on Active, our registration and payment platform, and add your child's profile to your account.

 Step 3: Complete the transaction on Active. 

 If you need help, please write to us using our contact form or call us at 514-687-9622 , ext. 1524 (Montréal) or 1-833-505-9622, ext. 1524 (outside Montréal). 

 Opening hours
 Monday - Friday* : 8 a.m. - 7 p.m. 
 Saturday* : 9 a.m. - 4 p.m.
 Sunday* : 10 a.m. - 4 p.m.
 View the itinerary 

 Our address

 673 Saint-Elmire Street
Saint-Sauveur-des-Monts, QC, J0R 1R1

 Phone numbers

 1 833 505-9622 
 514 687-9622 

 Email

 camp.kanawana@ymcaquebec.org 

 *Opening hours of the Contact Centre 

 Additional information

 Learn more about the program 

 Campers spend most days in our Regular Residential Camp program while also preparing and training for their 4- to 6-day canoe-tripping expedition.

 All our canoe trips are centred on teamwork and community living while helping participants develop their leadership and outdoor survival skills.

 Please note: For safety purposes, Camp YMCA Kanawana reserves the right to change the length and locations of each trip. These will be determined depending on weather, water, and road conditions, as well as the overall schedule of trips each session.

 Canoe trips are physically demanding and require a certain level of swimming ability. Kanawana therefore reserves the right to refuse any participant we deem unable to cope with the demands of such a trip.

 * If your child is gender non-conforming or transgender, please let us know so that we can ensure that they are comfortable with their cabin arrangement.

 A typical day at camp YMCA Kanawana 

 A wide range of activities every day.

 7:15 a.m. - 7:45 a.m.: Morning dip (optional)

 8:00 a.m. - 9:00 a.m.: Breakfast and announcements

 9:00 a.m. - 9:20 a.m.:  Cabin clean-up & preparation for the day

 9:20 a.m. - 10:25 a.m.:  Cabin/tent program #1

 10:25 a.m. - 11:30 a.m.:  Cabin/tent program #2

 11:30 a.m. - 12:15 p.m.: General swim and open program areas * (canoe, archery and nature activities)

 12:15 p.m. - 12:30 p.m.: Prepare for lunch

 12:30 p.m. - 1:30 p.m.: Lunch and announcements, plus section cheers every few days

 1:30 p.m. - 2:30 p.m.: Siesta/break time

 2:30 p.m. - 3:30 p.m.: Interest group #1

 3:30 p.m. - 4:30 p.m.: Interest group #2

 4:30 p.m. - 5:30 p.m.: General swim and open program areas *

 5:30 p.m. - 5:45 p.m.: Prepare for dinner

 5:45 p.m. - 6:45 p.m.: Dinner and announcements

 6:45 p.m. - 7:00 p.m.: Down time, no programming

 7:00 p.m. - 8:00 p.m.: Cabin/tent program #3

 8:00 p.m. - 9:00 p.m.: Cabin/tent program #4 (junior campers prepare for bed)

 9:00 p.m. - 10:00 p.m.: Campfire (senior campers prepare for bed)

 10:00 p.m.: Lights out

 * Open program areas vary depending on weather and availability of staff, but typically will change from morning to afternoon.

 Please note: Some days include all-section or all-camp activities instead of interest group blocks or cabin/tent group programming.

 Lights out time also varies depending on the daily activities and the age of the campers.

 Our schedule and programming is subject to change.

 Financial assistance 

 All young people should have the opportunity to experience the magic of camp, regardless of their financial situation. 

 That is why our financial assistance program can cover part of the cost if you are unable to pay the full amount. 

 Tax credits 

 Some fees are eligible for tax credits for child care expense and children’s physical activities. If you would like to receive the tax credit for child care expenses by advance payments , please consult the detailed procedure on the Revenu Québec website before contacting us. Certain conditions apply.

 Terms and conditions 

 Consult our terms and conditions to learn about our refund policies, Camp YMCA Kanawana registration modifications, as well as the general terms and conditions you agree to when you register your child for camp.

 Camps

 Discover Kanawana

 Coureurs des Bois (Ages 13 to 16)

 12-Day Coureurs des bois

 Campers aged 13 to 16 enjoy a stay filled with adventure, discovery and shared experiences at Camp YMCA Kanawana. 

 Through outdoor activities, community living and challenges, each day is an opportunity to develop new skills, build independence and form connections with others. 

 A one-night camping excursion on the shores of one of the camp’s three lakes enriches their experience and gives them an even greater taste of life in the great outdoors.  

 Learn more about the program 

 2027 registration

 Ages: 13 to 16

 Gender: boy and non-binary

 Registration for the 2027 season at YMCA Kanawana Camp is about to open!

 Fill out the interest form

 Previous element 

 Next element 

 Experience Kanawana to the Fullest

 Our Coureurs des bois Program at the Heart of Our Camp

 During their stay, campers enjoy a varied program that combines outdoor activities, water sports, arts, nature exploration, and group activities. Each day gives them opportunities to try new things, develop their independence, and build connections in an inclusive and supportive environment.

 Learn more about Stays at camp programs 

 Previous element 

 Next element 

 Additional information

 Learn more about the program 

 Campers spend most days in our Regular Residential Camp program while also preparing and training for their 4- to 6-day canoe camping trip.

 All our canoe trips are centred on teamwork and community living while helping participants develop their leadership and outdoor survival skills.

 Please note: For safety purposes, Camp YMCA Kanawana reserves the right to change the length and locations of each trip. These will be determined depending on weather, water, and road conditions, as well as the overall schedule of trips each session.

 Canoe trips are physically demanding and require a certain level of swimming ability. Kanawana therefore reserves the right to refuse any participant we deem unable to cope with the demands of such a trip.

 * If your child is gender non-conforming or transgender, please let us know so that we can ensure that they are comfortable with their cabin arrangement.

 A typical day at camp YMCA Kanawana 

 A wide range of activities every day.

 7:15 a.m. - 7:45 a.m.: Morning dip (optional)

 8:00 a.m. - 9:00 a.m.: Breakfast and announcements

 9:00 a.m. - 9:20 a.m.:  Cabin clean-up & preparation for the day

 9:20 a.m. - 10:25 a.m.:  Cabin/tent program #1

 10:25 a.m. - 11:30 a.m.:  Cabin/tent program #2

 11:30 a.m. - 12:15 p.m.: General swim and open program areas * (canoe, archery and nature activities)

 12:15 p.m. - 12:30 p.m.: Prepare for lunch

 12:30 p.m. - 1:30 p.m.: Lunch and announcements, plus section cheers every few days

 1:30 p.m. - 2:30 p.m.: Siesta/break time

 2:30 p.m. - 3:30 p.m.: Interest group #1

 3:30 p.m. - 4:30 p.m.: Interest group #2

 4:30 p.m. - 5:30 p.m.: General swim and open program areas *

 5:30 p.m. - 5:45 p.m.: Prepare for dinner

 5:45 p.m. - 6:45 p.m.: Dinner and announcements

 6:45 p.m. - 7:00 p.m.: Down time, no programming

 7:00 p.m. - 8:00 p.m.: Cabin/tent program #3

 8:00 p.m. - 9:00 p.m.: Cabin/tent program #4 (junior campers prepare for bed)

 9:00 p.m. - 10:00 p.m.: Campfire (senior campers prepare for bed)

 10:00 p.m.: Lights out

 * Open program areas vary depending on weather and availability of staff, but typically will change from morning to afternoon.

 Please note: Some days include all-section or all-camp activities instead of interest group blocks or cabin/tent group programming.

 Lights out time also varies depending on the daily activities and the age of the campers.

 Our schedule and programming is subject to change.

 Financial assistance 

 All young people should have the opportunity to experience the magic of camp, regardless of their financial situation. 

 That is why our financial assistance program can cover part of the cost if you are unable to pay the full amount. 

 Tax credits 

 Some fees are eligible for tax credits for child care expense and children’s physical activities. If you would like to receive the tax credit for child care expenses by advance payments , please consult the detailed procedure on the Revenu Québec website before contacting us. Certain conditions apply.

 Terms and conditions 

 Consult our terms and conditions to learn about our refund policies, Camp YMCA Kanawana registration modifications, as well as the general terms and conditions you agree to when you register your child for camp.

 Find out more about YMCA Kanawana camp

 All our practical advice for your stay at camp.

 Camps

 Discover Kanawana

 12-Day Pathfinders (Ages 13-16)

 12-Day Pathfinders

 Campers aged 13 to 16 enjoy the full Camp YMCA Kanawana experience through outdoor activities, challenges, discoveries and shared experiences with their group. 

 During their stay, they build independence, form new connections and enjoy everything camp life has to offer. 

 A one-night camping excursion on the shores of one of the camp’s three lakes rounds out the adventure and gives them an even more immersive experience in the great outdoors.  

 2027 registration

 Ages: 13 to 16

 Gender: girl and non-binary

 Registration for the 2027 season at YMCA Kanawana Camp is about to open!

 Fill out the interest form

 Previous element 

 Next element 

 Experience Kanawana to the Fullest

 Our Pathfinders Program at the Heart of Our Camp

 During their stay, campers enjoy a varied program that combines outdoor activities, water sports, arts, nature exploration, and group activities. Each day gives them opportunities to try new things, develop their independence, and build connections in an inclusive and supportive environment.

 Learn more about Stays at camp programs

 Additional information

 A typical day at camp

 Home

 Camps

 Discover Kanawana

 12-Day Explorers Pioneers (Ages 11 to 12)

 12-Day Explorers Pioneers

 Campers aged 11 to 12 enjoy an experience that combines life at Camp YMCA Kanawana with a multiday wilderness adventure. 

 Alongside camp activities, Explorers prepare for a four-day camping trip in the Papineau-Labelle Wildlife Reserve combining canoeing and hiking. 

 The experience is designed to build independence and develop their team spirit and outdoor skills while helping them take on new challenges.  

 2027 registration

 Ages: 11 to 12

 Gender: girl and non-binary

 Registration for the 2027 season at YMCA Kanawana Camp is about to open!

 Fill out the interest form

 Previous element 

 Next element 

 Experience a Canoe-Camping Adventure

 Our Explorers Pioneers program in the heart of nature

 Guided by an experienced team, campers set off on a canoe-camping adventure and experience life in the great outdoors. Paddling, setting up camp, cooking together, and sharing stories around the campfire are all part of the journey. It’s an immersive experience that lets them discover remarkable landscapes while building independence, teamwork, and self-confidence.

 Learn more about canoe-camping expeditions 

 Previous element 

 Next element 

 Additional information

 A typical day at camp 

 This is a typical day on a canoe-tripping expedition:
7 a.m.: wake-up
7:30 a.m.: participation in tasks that will also need to be done on the trip, such as gathering firewood and making breakfast
9 a.m.: take down tents and camp site and help pack canoes
10:30 a.m.: paddle
11:30 a.m.: canoe games and rest
12:30 p.m.: lunch on the beach
2 p.m.: paddle to camp site
3 p.m.: put up tents and swimming by camp site
4 p.m.: survival program activity     
5:30 p.m.: dinner preparation and participation in trip tasks
7:30 p.m.: stories around the campfire
9 p.m.: teeth brushing and sweet dreams

 Please note that this is a generic schedule that will be adapted to each program by our trip guides according to the group's itinerary. 

 Financial assistance 

 All young people should have the opportunity to experience the magic of camp, regardless of their financial situation. That is why our financial assistance program can cover part of the cost if you are unable to pay the full amount. 

 Tax credits 

 Some fees are eligible for tax credits for child care expense and children’s physical activities. If you would like to receive the tax credit for child care expenses by advance payments , please consult the detailed procedure on the Revenu Québec website before contacting us. Certain conditions apply.

 Terms and conditions 

 Consult our terms and conditions to learn about our refund policies, Camp YMCA Kanawana registration modifications, as well as the general terms and conditions you agree to when you register your child for camp.

 Find out more about YMCA Kanawana camp

 All our practical advice for your stay at camp.

 Camps

 Discover Kanawana

 12-Day Explorers Woodsies (Ages 11 to 12)

 12-Day Explorers Woodsies

 During a 12-day stay, campers aged 11 to 12 enjoy an experience that combines life at Camp YMCA Kanawana with a multiday wilderness adventure. 

 Alongside camp activities, Explorers prepare for a four-day camping trip in the Papineau-Labelle Wildlife Reserve combining canoeing and hiking. 

 This is an opportunity to build independence and develop their team spirit and outdoor skills while taking on new challenges.  

 2027 registration

 Ages: 11 to 12

 Gender: Boy and non-binary

 Registration for the 2027 season at YMCA Kanawana Camp is about to open!

 Fill out the interest form

 Previous element 

 Next element 

 Experience a Canoe-Camping Adventure

 Our Explorers Woodsies program in the heart of nature

 Guided by an experienced team, campers set off on a canoe-camping adventure and experience life in the great outdoors. Paddling, setting up camp, cooking together, and sharing stories around the campfire are all part of the journey. It’s an immersive experience that lets them discover remarkable landscapes while building independence, teamwork, and self-confidence.

 Learn more about canoe-camping expeditions 

 Previous element 

 Next element 

 Additional information

 A typical day at camp 

 This is a typical day on a canoe-tripping expedition:
7 a.m.: wake-up
7:30 a.m.: participation in tasks that will also need to be done on the trip, such as gathering firewood and making breakfast
9 a.m.: take down tents and camp site and help pack canoes
10:30 a.m.: paddle
11:30 a.m.: canoe games and rest
12:30 p.m.: lunch on the beach
2 p.m.: paddle to camp site
3 p.m.: put up tents and swimming by camp site
4 p.m.: survival program activity     
5:30 p.m.: dinner preparation and participation in trip tasks
7:30 p.m.: stories around the campfire
9 p.m.: teeth brushing and sweet dreams

 Please note that this is a generic schedule that will be adapted to each program by our trip guides according to the group's itinerary. 

 Financial assistance 

 All young people should have the opportunity to experience the magic of camp, regardless of their financial situation. That is why our financial assistance program can cover part of the cost if you are unable to pay the full amount. 

 Tax credits 

 Some fees are eligible for tax credits for child care expense and children’s physical activities. If you would like to receive the tax credit for child care expenses by advance payments , please consult the detailed procedure on the Revenu Québec website before contacting us. Certain conditions apply.

 Terms and conditions 

 Consult our terms and conditions to learn about our refund policies, Camp YMCA Kanawana registration modifications, as well as the general terms and conditions you agree to when you register your child for camp.

 All our practical advice for your stay at camp.

 Home

 Camps

 Discover Kanawana

 6-Day Pioneers (Ages 7-12)

 6-Day Pioneers

 During a six-day stay, campers aged 7 to 12 discover life at Camp YMCA Kanawana in a welcoming and well-supervised setting. 

 Water activities, outdoor adventures, creative pursuits and time spent with their group give them opportunities to try new activities, build independence and form new connections. 

 This shorter stay is ideal for experiencing Kanawana for the first time and enjoying camp life to the fullest.  

 2027 registration

 Ages: 7 to 12

 Gender: girl and non-binary

 Registration for the 2027 season at YMCA Kanawana Camp is about to open!

 Fill out the interest form

 Previous element 

 Next element 

 Experience Kanawana to the Fullest

 Our Pioneers program at the heart of our camp

 During their stay, campers enjoy a varied program that combines outdoor activities, water sports, arts, nature exploration, and group activities. Each day gives them opportunities to try new things, develop their independence, and build connections in an inclusive and supportive environment.

 Learn more about Stays at camp programs 

 Previous element 

 Next element 

 Useful information

 A typical day at camp 

 A wide range of activities every day.

 7:15 a.m. - 7:45 a.m.: Morning dip (optional)
8:00 a.m. - 9:00 a.m.: Breakfast and announcements
9:00 a.m. - 9:20 a.m.:  Cabin clean-up & preparation for the day
9:20 a.m. - 10:25 a.m.:  Cabin/tent program #1
10:25 a.m. - 11:30 a.m.:  Cabin/tent program #2
11:30 a.m. - 12:15 p.m.: General swim and open program areas * (canoe, archery and nature activities)
12:15 p.m. - 12:30 p.m.: Prepare for lunch
12:30 p.m. - 1:30 p.m.: Lunch and announcements, plus section cheers every few days
1:30 p.m. - 2:30 p.m.: Siesta/break time
2:30 p.m. - 3:30 p.m.: Interest group #1
3:30 p.m. - 4:30 p.m.: Interest group #2
4:30 p.m. - 5:30 p.m.: General swim and open program areas *
5:30 p.m. - 5:45 p.m.: Prepare for dinner
5:45 p.m. - 6:45 p.m.: Dinner and announcements
6:45 p.m. - 7:00 p.m.: Down time, no programming
7:00 p.m. - 8:00 p.m.: Cabin/tent program #3
8:00 p.m. - 9:00 p.m.: Cabin/tent program #4 (junior campers prepare for bed)
9:00 p.m. - 10:00 p.m.: Campfire (senior campers prepare for bed)
10:00 p.m.: Lights out

 * Open program areas vary depending on weather and availability of staff, but typically will change from morning to afternoon.

 Please note: Some days include all-section or all-camp activities instead of interest group blocks or cabin/tent group programming.
Lights out time also varies depending on the daily activities and the age of the campers.
Our schedule and programming is subject to change.

 Financial assistance 

 All young people should have the opportunity to experience the magic of camp, regardless of their financial situation. That is why our financial assistance program can cover part of the cost if you are unable to pay the full amount. 

 Tax credits 

 Some fees are eligible for tax credits for child care expense and children’s physical activities. If you would like to receive the tax credit for child care expenses by advance payments , please consult the detailed procedure on the Revenu Québec website before contacting us. Certain conditions apply.

 Terms and conditions 

 Consult our terms and conditions to learn about our refund policies, Camp YMCA Kanawana registration modifications, as well as the general terms and conditions you agree to when you register your child for camp.

 Find out more about YMCA Kanawana camp

 All our practical advice for your stay at camp.

 Discover Kanawana

 12-Day Pioneers (Ages 7-12)

 12-Day Pioneers

 During a 12-day stay, campers aged 7 to 12 experience life at Camp YMCA Kanawana to the fullest in a welcomi ng, well-supervised setting.  

 With water activities, outdoor adventures, creative activities and shared experiences with their group, each day is an opportunity to explore, build independence and form new connections.  

 An age-appropriate trip rounds out their stay: a day trip for younger campers and, for older campers, the opportunity to spend a night on the shores of one of the camp’s three lakes. 

 2027 registration

 Ages: 7 to 12

 Gender: girl and non-binary

 Registration for the 2027 season at YMCA Kanawana Camp is about to open!

 Fill out the interest form

 Previous element 

 Next element

 Our Pioneers program at the heart of our camp

 During their stay, campers enjoy a varied program that combines outdoor activities, water sports, arts, nature exploration, and group activities. Each day gives them opportunities to try new things, develop their independence, and build connections in an inclusive and supportive environment.

 Additional information

 A typical day at camp YMCA Kanawana 

 A wide range of activities every day.

 7:15 a.m. - 7:45 a.m.: Morning dip (optional)

 8:00 a.m. - 9:00 a.m.: Breakfast and announcements

 9:00 a.m. - 9:20 a.m.:  Cabin clean-up & preparation for the day

 9:20 a.m. - 10:25 a.m.:  Cabin/tent program #1

 10:25 a.m. - 11:30 a.m.:  Cabin/tent program #2

 11:30 a.m. - 12:15 p.m.: General swim and open program areas * (canoe, archery and nature activities)

 12:15 p.m. - 12:30 p.m.: Prepare for lunch

 12:30 p.m. - 1:30 p.m.: Lunch and announcements, plus section cheers every few days

 1:30 p.m. - 2:30 p.m.: Siesta/break time

 2:30 p.m. - 3:30 p.m.: Interest group #1

 3:30 p.m. - 4:30 p.m.: Interest group #2

 4:30 p.m. - 5:30 p.m.: General swim and open program areas *

 5:30 p.m. - 5:45 p.m.: Prepare for dinner

 5:45 p.m. - 6:45 p.m.: Dinner and announcements

 6:45 p.m. - 7:00 p.m.: Down time, no programming

 7:00 p.m. - 8:00 p.m.: Cabin/tent program #3

 8:00 p.m. - 9:00 p.m.: Cabin/tent program #4 (junior campers prepare for bed)

 9:00 p.m. - 10:00 p.m.: Campfire (senior campers prepare for bed)

 10:00 p.m.: Lights out

 * Open program areas vary depending on weather and availability of staff, but typically will change from morning to afternoon.

 Please note: Some days include all-section or all-camp activities instead of interest group blocks or cabin/tent group programming.

 Lights out time also varies depending on the daily activities and the age of the campers.

 Our schedule and programming is subject to change.

 Financial assistance 

 All young people should have the opportunity to experience the magic of camp, regardless of their financial situation. 

 That is why our financial assistance program can cover part of the cost if you are unable to pay the full amount. 

 Tax credits 

 Some fees are eligible for tax credits for child care expense and children’s physical activities. If you would like to receive the tax credit for child care expenses by advance payments , please consult the detailed procedure on the Revenu Québec website before contacting us. Certain conditions apply.

 Terms and conditions 

 Consult our terms and conditions to learn about our refund policies, Camp YMCA Kanawana registration modifications, as well as the general terms and conditions you agree to when you register your child for camp.

 Find out more about YMCA Kanawana camp

 All our practical advice for your stay at camp.

 Home

 Camps

 Discover Kanawana

 6-Day Woodsies (Ages 7-12)

 6-Day Woodsies

 During a six-day stay, campers aged 7 to 12 get their first taste of life at Camp YMCA Kanawana in a welcoming and well-supervised setting. 

 With water activities, outdoor adventures, discoveries and shared experiences with their group, each day is an opportunity to try new things, build independence and have fun. 

 This shorter program is ideal for discovering camp life and experiencing time away from home for the first time.  

 Information

 Ages: 7 to 12

 Gender: boy and non-binary

 Registration for the 2027 season at YMCA Kanawana Camp is about to open!

 Fill out the interest form

 Previous element 

 Next element 

 Experience Kanawana to the Fullest

 Our Woodsies Program at the Heart of Our Camp

 During their stay, campers enjoy a varied program that combines outdoor activities, water sports, arts, nature exploration, and group activities. Each day gives them opportunities to try new things, develop their independence, and build connections in an inclusive and supportive environment.

 Learn more about Stays at camp programs 

 Previous element 

 Next element 

 Useful Information

 A Typical Day at Camp YMCA Kanawana 

 A wide range of activities every day.

 7:15 a.m. - 7:45 a.m.: Morning dip (optional)

 8:00 a.m. - 9:00 a.m.: Breakfast and announcements

 9:00 a.m. - 9:20 a.m.:  Cabin clean-up & preparation for the day

 9:20 a.m. - 10:25 a.m.:  Cabin/tent program #1

 10:25 a.m. - 11:30 a.m.:  Cabin/tent program #2

 11:30 a.m. - 12:15 p.m.: General swim and open program areas * (canoe, archery and nature activities)

 12:15 p.m. - 12:30 p.m.: Prepare for lunch

 12:30 p.m. - 1:30 p.m.: Lunch and announcements, plus section cheers every few days

 1:30 p.m. - 2:30 p.m.: Siesta/break time

 2:30 p.m. - 3:30 p.m.: Interest group #1

 3:30 p.m. - 4:30 p.m.: Interest group #2

 4:30 p.m. - 5:30 p.m.: General swim and open program areas *

 5:30 p.m. - 5:45 p.m.: Prepare for dinner

 5:45 p.m. - 6:45 p.m.: Dinner and announcements

 6:45 p.m. - 7:00 p.m.: Down time, no programming

 7:00 p.m. - 8:00 p.m.: Cabin/tent program #3

 8:00 p.m. - 9:00 p.m.: Cabin/tent program #4 (junior campers prepare for bed)

 9:00 p.m. - 10:00 p.m.: Campfire (senior campers prepare for bed)

 10:00 p.m.: Lights out

 * Open program areas vary depending on weather and availability of staff, but typically will change from morning to afternoon.

 Please note: Some days include all-section or all-camp activities instead of interest group blocks or cabin/tent group programming.

 Lights out time also varies depending on the daily activities and the age of the campers.

 Our schedule and programming is subject to change.

 Changeovers 

 This option is open for campers aged 7 to 16 and offers an array of activities that are supervised by at least 2 staff members and a member of our summer camp management team.

 On top of enjoying quieter camp time, campers will have the opportunity (weather dependent) to partake in a day of activities at Sommet Saint-Sauveur, a well-known water park located 10 minutes away from camp, or go bowling if the weather turns bad. On top of providing meals, snacks and supervision, our changeover campers will also benefit from a laundry service to wash their belongings between sessions. Campers that stay changeover at Camp YMCA Kanawana will also have the opportunity to call home during the weekend.

 From July 4 to July 6, 2025 
3 days – 2 nights
Price: $397 + tax

 Register your child for changeovers 

 Financial Assistance 

 All young people should have the opportunity to experience the magic of camp, regardless of their financial situation. 

 That is why our financial assistance program can cover part of the cost if you are unable to pay the full amount. 

 Tax Credits 

 Some fees are eligible for tax credits for child care expense and children’s physical activities. If you would like to receive the tax credit for child care expenses by advance payments , please consult the detailed procedure on the Revenu Québec website before contacting us. Certain conditions apply.

 Terms and Conditions 

 Consult our terms and conditions to learn about our refund policies, Camp YMCA Kanawana registration modifications, as well as the general terms and conditions you agree to when you register your child for camp.

 Home

 Camps

 Discover Kanawana

 12-Day Woodsies (Ages 7 to 12)

 12-Day Woodsies

 In the heart of nature, campers aged 7 to 12 enjoy the full Kanawana experience in a welcoming and well-supervised setting. 

 Swimming, canoeing, outdoor activities, creative pursuits and time spent with their group fill their days, helping them build independence and develop new skills while having fun. 

 An age-appropriate trip rounds out the adventure: a day trip for younger campers aged 7 to 9, while older campers have the opportunity to spend a night on the shores of one of the camp’s three lakes.  

 2027 registration

 Ages: 7 to 12

 Gender: boy and non-binary

 Registration for the 2027 season at YMCA Kanawana Camp is about to open!

 Fill out the interest form

 Previous element 

 Next element
